start-training.description: Spins up an isolated branch named with the current date and time
start-training.template:
I am ready to start my training lifecycle. Run a local bash script to execute these sequential steps precisely:
1. git checkout main
2. git checkout -b training-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
Then, read my agents.md rules and explicitly tell me: 'Branch created. Initiate the interview.'

resume-training.description: Restores the mentor's context by analyzing the active codebase and session state
resume-training.template: I am resuming my training session on this active branch. Please read my .opencode/session.json file from disk, look at my progress.md checklist, and scan my current Java codebase in src/main/java/com/bootcamp/ to understand my pending implementation. Tell me exactly what my current task is and where I should focus right now.

hint.description: Requests a tier-appropriate conceptual clue without exposing the code solution
hint.template: I am stuck on the current exercise. Based on my interview level recorded in .opencode/session.json, provide a conceptual hint or architectural advice. Do not reveal any code solutions.

submit-exercise.description: Compiles code, runs Maven tests, logs progress, and creates an atomic Git commit
submit-exercise.template:
Validate my solution by performing these step-by-step local operations:
1. Run the terminal command: mvn test
2. If tests pass, read progress.md and mark the current completed exercise as [x]
3. Read .opencode/session.json, update 'last_completed_milestone' to the completed topic name and increment 'sessions_completed' by 1, then save the file
4. Stage all project files using: git add .
5. Create a local git commit with a descriptive message: git commit -m 'feat: complete <topic name>'
6. Print a final message to the user: 'Progress securely committed locally!'
